Visit note | 2025-06-07 03:00 PM | Dr. Zahid Hasan, Gastroenterology | Patient: Babul Dewan, 32, male. Mr. Dewan comes for a follow-up visit reporting a burning sensation behind his breastbone after meals, a sour taste in his mouth, and that his symptoms become worse when he lies down. He mentions this has been worse after weeks of fried snacks at tea stalls in Narayanganj. He works as a construction worker. He has Bronchial asthma. He reports no difficulty swallowing or unintended weight loss. Examination reveals BMI 32.5, BP 111/84 mmHg, pulse 77 bpm, and weight 53 kg. Abdominal examination is soft with mild epigastric tenderness. Assessment: Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease. Plan: a prescription was issued today. He was advised to eat smaller meals, avoid oily and spicy food late at night, and raise the head of the bed. Follow-up is scheduled in 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-06-07 03:00 PM | Dr. Mahbuba Rahman, Psychiatry | Patient: Dalia Molla, 39, female. Mrs. Molla attends for her review, describing sudden attacks of a racing heart and breathlessness during these episodes, though her heart tests remain normal. She notes her first attack happened in a crowded lift in Savar and reports having about 10 panic attacks in the last month. Her occupation is a restaurant cook. She has a history of Hypothyroidism. She denies chest pain radiating to the arm or jaw. On examination, her vital signs show BP 119/86 mmHg, pulse 80 bpm, and weight 78 kg. She appears anxious but is fully oriented. Assessment: Panic disorder. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to practise slow breathing during attacks, reduce caffeine intake, and start counselling sessions. Follow-up is in 4 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-06-07 03:30 PM | Dr. Kamrul Hasan, Pulmonology | Patient: Fahim Talukder, 67, male. Mr. Talukder returns for review with a long history of smoking and producing more sputum than usual, which worsened during the dusty dry season in Gulshan. He works as a tailor. He has no reported comorbidities. He denies fever or sharp pleuritic chest pain. Clinical examination records SpO2 89%, BP 111/83 mmHg, pulse 89 bpm, and weight 74 kg. Chest auscultation reveals bilateral wheezes and prolonged expiration. Assessment: COPD exacerbation. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to stop smoking completely, avoid cooking smoke, and take the yearly flu vaccine. Follow-up is in 1 week, or sooner if his breathing worsens.

Visit note | 2025-06-07 03:30 PM | Dr. Lubna Rahman, Endocrinology | Patient: Ehsan Faruque, 20, male. He has a comorbidity of Essential hypertension. He denies significant weight loss or palpitations at rest. Examination findings include pulse 121 bpm, BP 151/91 mmHg, and weight 60 kg. Follow-up is in 4 weeks with thyroid function tests.

Visit note | 2025-06-07 03:30 PM | Dr. Mehedi Hasan, Ophthalmology | Patient: Rumana Gazi, 73, female. Examination shows tear break-up time 7 seconds, BP 122/71 mmHg, pulse 91 bpm, and weight 61 kg. Cornea is clear with mild conjunctival injection. Assessment: Dry eye syndrome. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to look away from the screen every 20 minutes, blink often, and use a humidifier. Follow-up is in 1 month.

Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to avoid dust and smoke, keep the bedroom well aired, and learn the correct inhaler technique. Follow-up is in 1 month to check inhaler technique.

Visit note | 2025-06-08 10:00 AM | Dr. Mahbuba Rahman, Psychiatry | Patient: Tasnim Khatun, 54, female. Mrs. Khatun visits for a follow-up regarding poor sleep and low mood for over three weeks.
